# Pico AI Bot Interposer Build

Rev 0.4 10/15/26

This documentation is provided for remote participants in the DPRG’s “Learn to program a robot using AI” workshop. It shows how to build the interposer used in the workshop. It should enable remote attendees to build the necessary hardware to participate in the Winky-Blinky Challenge.

You do not need the robot connector shown unless you intend to connect to your own robot. You will be able to participate in the Winky-Blinky challenge using only two LEDs and a Pico.

# Parts Required

* Raspberry Pi Pico with headers  
* Data-capable micro-USB cable  
* Perf board or proto board or solderless breadboard  
* Pin sockets if using proto board \- 5 pins minimum for each side of the Pico  
* 2 Resistors \- any value in the 100 ohm to 680 ohm range  
* 2 LEDs \- any color  
* 1N5817 Schottky diode (optional \- see note on schematic)  
* Wire, solder

# Schematic

**![][image1]**  
**Note:** if you will be connecting the USB cable to the interposer board concurrently with it being plugged into a robot, you will need a schottky diode such as 1N5817 to prevent USB power from back-feeding into the robot battery.
